s: idol worship is practiced by lovers of evil things (those who make, desire, and worship idols)

s: idol worship includes worship of hateful creatures (worse than all others in lack of sense)
q: Yes, and they worship the creatures that are most hateful, for, being compared as to lack of sense, these are worse than all others;

s: God is patient
q: But you, our God, are gracious and true, patient, and in mercy ordering all things.

s: God orders all things (in mercy)
q: But you, our God, are gracious and true, patient, and in mercy ordering all things.

s: God molded man (inspired an active soul and breathed a vital spirit into him)
q: because he was ignorant of him who molded him, and of him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed into him a vital spirit.

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) belongs to God (even if they sin)
q: For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your dominion; but we will not sin, knowing that we have been accounted yours.

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) knows God's dominion
q: For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your dominion;

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) was not led astray by idol worship (by evil plan of men or painters' labor)
q: For we weren’t led astray by any evil plan of men’s, nor yet by painters’ fruitless labor, a form stained with varied colors,

s: potter is a maker of clay vessels
q: For a potter, kneading soft earth, laboriously molds each article for our service.

s: God is a Savior of all
q: but because of you, the Savior of all.

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) trusts God
q: your word preserves those who trust you.

s: Egyptians is punished by vermin (deservedly, through creatures like those they worship)
q: they were deservedly punished through creatures like those which they worship, and tormented through a multitude of vermin.

s: Egyptians is a oppressors
q: inescapable lack should come upon those oppressors

s: Egyptians is a ungodly men (refusing to know God)
q: for ungodly men, refusing to know you, were scourged

s: vermin torments Egyptians
q: tormented through a multitude of vermin.

s: quails is a delicacy (food satisfying appetite)
q: prepared quails for food, a delicacy to satisfy the desire of their appetite,

s: quails is sent for God's people (Israel, your sons) (as food)
q: you, giving benefits to your people, prepared quails for food

s: angels' food (bread from heaven) has property every pleasant flavor (agreeable to every taste)
q: having the virtue of every pleasant flavor, and agreeable to every taste.

s: angels' food (bread from heaven) changes according to every man's choice (serving the desire of the eater)
q: that bread, serving the desire of the eater, changed itself according to every man’s choice.

s: angels' food (bread from heaven) comes from heaven (provided without toil)
q: you provided ready-to-eat bread for them from heaven without toil

s: God has authority over life and death
q: For you have authority over life and death, and you lead down to the gates of Hades, and lead up again.

s: storms of hail, rain and fire punishes Egyptians (strange rains, hails and relentless storms with fire)
q: were scourged in the strength of your arm, pursued with strange rains and hails and relentless storms, and utterly consumed with fire.

s: storms of hail, rain and fire has property fire burns hotter in water (marvelous effect)
q: in the water which quenches all things, the fire burned hotter

s: creation serves God (ministers to its maker)
q: For the creation, ministering to you, its maker,

s: wild beasts and serpents harms God's people (Israel, your sons) (temporarily, for admonition)
q: For even when terrible raging of wild beasts came upon your people, and they were perishing by the bites of crooked serpents

s: locusts and flies kills Egyptians (no healing found)
q: For the bites of locusts and flies truly killed them.

s: God heals all people (through his word)
q: but your word, O Lord, which heals all people.

s: God loves God's people (Israel, your sons) (his children)
q: that your children, whom you loved, O Lord, might learn

s: God is creator of creation
q: For the creation, ministering to you, its maker,

s: God provides angels' food (bread from heaven) (for his people, without toil)
q: you gave your people angels’ food to eat, and you provided ready-to-eat bread for them from heaven without toil

s: God provides quails (as food for his people)
q: you, giving benefits to your people, prepared quails for food, a delicacy to satisfy the desire of their appetite,

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) is a children of God
q: But your children weren’t overcome by the very fangs of venomous dragons

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) receives angels' food (bread from heaven) (nourishment from heaven)
q: you gave your people angels’ food to eat

s: God's judgments has attribute great
q: For your judgments are great, and hard to interpret

s: fear is a surrender of the help which reason offers
q: For fear is nothing else but a surrender of the help which reason offers;

s: darkness is a image of the darkness that should afterward receive them (heavy night over them alone)
q: over them alone was spread a heavy night, an image of the darkness that should afterward receive them

s: God's judgments has attribute hard to interpret
q: For your judgments are great, and hard to interpret

s: lawless men is a undisciplined souls (went astray)
q: therefore undisciplined souls went astray.

s: lawless men supposed to hold holy nation (in their power)
q: For when lawless men had supposed that they held a holy nation in their power

s: lawless men is state prisoners of darkness
q: they, prisoners of darkness, and bound in the fetters of a long night

s: lawless men is state exiled from eternal providence
q: lay exiled from the eternal providence.

s: lawless men is state divided from one another (by a dark curtain of forgetfulness)
q: they were divided from one another by a dark curtain of forgetfulness

s: God provides pillar of fire (guide for the people's unknown journey)
q: Therefore you provided a burning pillar of fire, to be a guide for your people’s unknown journey, and a harmless sun for their glorious exile.

s: death of the firstborn causes Egyptians (confessed the people to be God's children)
q: upon the destruction of the firstborn they confessed the people to be God’s children.

s: Egyptians disbelieve enchantments (disbelieved all things by reason of enchantments)
q: For while they were disbelieving all things by reason of the enchantments

s: wilderness plague touches God's people (Israel, your sons) (multitude destroyed in the wilderness; wrath short-lived)
q: The experience of death also touched the righteous, and a multitude were destroyed in the wilderness, but the wrath didn’t last long.

s: blameless man (Aaron) is a servant of God
q: showing that he was your servant.

s: blameless man (Aaron) has ministry (weapon of prayer and atoning incense)
q: bringing the weapon of his own ministry, prayer, and the atoning sacrifice of incense.

s: blameless man (Aaron) wears high priest's robe (world pictured on it)
q: For the whole world was pictured on his long robe

s: blameless man (Aaron) stops wilderness plague (by his word, recalling oaths and covenants with the fathers)

s: Egyptians deserve deprivation of light (imprisoned by darkness)
q: For the Egyptians well deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned by darkness

s: Egyptians imprison God's people (Israel, your sons) (children of God)
q: they who had imprisoned your children

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) is a children of God
q: they who had imprisoned your children, through whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given to the race of men.

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) gives light of the law (to the race of men; destined role)
q: through whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given to the race of men.

s: God destroys Egyptians (army destroyed in a mighty flood)
q: you took away from them their multitude of children, and destroyed all their army together in a mighty flood.

s: God's people (Israel, your sons) agree to covenant of the divine law (share the same good things and perils)
q: with one consent they agreed to the covenant of the divine law, that they would partake alike in the same good things and the same perils

s: death of the firstborn affects servant and master (same doom for all classes)
q: Both servant and master were punished with the same just doom, and the commoner suffering the same as king;

s: God foreknows future of the ungodly (God foreknew their change of mind)
q: for God also foreknew their future,

s: Egyptian pursuit of the Israelites has purpose fill up the punishment lacking from their torments (driven by deserved doom)
q: that they might fill up the punishment which was yet lacking from their torments,

s: creation complies with God (made new again, each part in its kind, to keep God's servants unharmed)
q: For the whole creation, each part in its diverse kind, was made new again, complying with your commandments, that your servants might be kept unharmed.

s: creation is compared to lute (elements change order like notes varying rhythm)
q: For as the notes of a lute vary the character of the rhythm, even so the elements, changing their order one with another

s: God magnifies God's people (Israelites) (in all things, standing by their side in every time and place)
q: For in all things, O Lord, you magnified your people, and you glorified them and didn’t lightly regard them, standing by their side in every time and place.

s: God is deliverer of God's people (Israelites) (praised by them as their deliverer)
q: praising you, O Lord, who was their deliverer.

s: God's people (Israelites) is covered by God (covered with God's hand)
q: these who were covered with your hand, having seen strange marvels.

s: Egyptians enslaved guests who were their benefactors (hatred toward guests)
q: the Egyptians made slaves of guests who were their benefactors.

s: Egyptians is a ungodly (subject of indignation without mercy)
q: But indignation without mercy came upon the ungodly to the end;

s: Egyptians suffers loss of sight (surrounded by yawning darkness)
q: they were stricken with loss of sight (even as were those others at the righteous man’s doors)

s: Red sea became unhindered highway (for God's people to pass over)
q: out of the Red sea an unhindered highway, and a grassy plain out of the violent surge,

s: Wisdom is a spirit who loves man
q: For wisdom is a spirit who loves man

s: judges of the earth is exhorted to love righteousness
q: Love righteousness, all you who are judges of the earth.

s: the ungodly summon death (by their hands and words)
q: ungodly men by their hands and their words summon death

s: the ungodly made covenant with death (worthy to belong with him)
q: They made a covenant with him, because they are worthy to belong with him.

s: death has no royal dominion earth (Hades)
q: nor has Hades royal dominion upon earth

s: righteousness is immortal
q: for righteousness is immortal,

s: creation has property wholesome generative powers (no poison of destruction in them)
q: The generative powers of the world are wholesome, and there is no poison of destruction in them

s: Wisdom does not enter soul that devises evil (will not enter or dwell)
q: because wisdom will not enter into a soul that devises evil, nor dwell in a body that is enslaved by sin.

s: Wisdom does not hold guiltless blasphemer (for his lips)
q: she will not hold a blasphemer guiltless for his lips

s: God is found by those who don’t put him to the test (also manifested to those who trust him)
q: he is found by those who don’t put him to the test, and is manifested to those who trust him.

s: God is witness of inmost self of a person (God as witness, overseer of heart, hearer of tongue)
q: God is witness of his inmost self, and is a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

s: God has spirit that fills the world
q: the spirit of the Lord has filled the world

s: God did not make death (does not delight when the living perish)
q: God didn’t make death, neither does he delight when the living perish.

s: God creates creation (so that all things might have being)
q: he created all things that they might have being.

s: God has attribute jealous ear (listens to all things)
q: a jealous ear listens to all things

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) believes life is short and ends in oblivion (unsound reasoning)
q: For they said within themselves, with unsound reasoning, “Our life is short and sorrowful.

s: the righteous man has way of life unlike other men's (strange paths)
q: because his life is unlike other men’s, and his paths are strange.

s: the righteous man abstains from the ways of the ungodly (as from uncleanness)
q: he abstains from our ways as from uncleanness.

s: the righteous man calls father God (boast)
q: He boasts that God is his father.

s: God created man (humanity created by God) (for incorruption)
q: Because God created man for incorruption, and made him an image of his own everlastingness;

s: death entered the world (by the envy of the devil)
q: but death entered into the world by the envy of the devil

s: enjoyment of pleasures (hedonistic revelry) includes costly wine and perfumes
q: Let’s fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes, and let no spring flower pass us by.

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) believes origin of humans mere chance
q: Because we were born by mere chance, and hereafter we will be as though we had never been

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) is led astray (blinded by their wickedness)
q: Thus they reasoned, and they were led astray; for their wickedness blinded them,

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) lacks knowledge of mysteries of God
q: and they didn’t know the mysteries of God, neither did they hope for wages of holiness

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) practices enjoyment of pleasures (hedonistic revelry) (claim it is their portion and lot)
q: because this is our portion, and this is our lot.

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) opposes the righteous man (he annoys them and reproaches their sins)
q: But let’s lie in wait for the righteous man, because he annoys us, is contrary to our works, reproaches us with sins against the law

s: the ungodly (those who speak in verses 1-20) oppresses the righteous poor (intended policy)
q: Let’s oppress the righteous poor.

s: the righteous man professes knowledge of God
q: He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord.

s: the righteous located in God (in his hand)
q: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them.

s: the ungodly neglects righteousness
q: those who neglected righteousness and revolted from the Lord;

s: the ungodly revolts from God
q: those who neglected righteousness and revolted from the Lord;

s: the ungodly has hope void
q: Their hope is void and their toils unprofitable. Their works are useless.

s: the ungodly has works useless
q: Their hope is void and their toils unprofitable. Their works are useless.

s: the righteous has state peace
q: but they are in peace.

s: parents of unlawfully conceived children will not reach maturity
q: But children of adulterers will not come to maturity.

s: parents of unlawfully conceived children has seed fate vanish away (seed of an unlawful union)
q: The seed of an unlawful union will vanish away.

s: parents of unlawfully conceived children has old age without honor (if they live long)
q: For if they live long, they will not be esteemed, and in the end, their old age will be without honor.

s: parents of unlawfully conceived children has no consolation in day of judgment (if they die young)
q: If they die young, they will have no hope, nor consolation in the day of judgment.

s: wisdom and discipline is despised by the ungodly (he who despises them is miserable)
q: for he who despises wisdom and discipline is miserable.

s: the righteous has hope immortality
q: their hope is full of immortality.

s: the righteous is tested by God (found worthy of himself)
q: because God tested them, and found them worthy of himself.

s: the righteous will judge nations and peoples (will have dominion over them)
q: They will judge nations and have dominion over peoples.

s: the righteous is ruled by God (forever)
q: The Lord will reign over them forever.

s: the righteous lives with God (in love, the faithful)
q: The faithful will live with him in love, because grace and mercy are with his chosen ones.

s: God has with chosen ones grace and mercy
q: because grace and mercy are with his chosen ones.

s: the ungodly receives punishment (according to their reasoning)
q: But the ungodly will be punished even as their reasoning deserves, those who neglected righteousness and revolted from the Lord;

s: virtue grants immortality (in its memory)
q: for immortality is in the memory of virtue

s: righteous man is found well-pleasing to God
q: Being found well-pleasing to God, someone was loved.

s: God visits righteous man (grace and mercy are with his chosen and holy ones)
q: grace and mercy are with his chosen, and that he visits his holy ones;

s: righteous man will condemn the ungodly (even when dead, condemns the living ungodly)
q: but a righteous man who is dead will condemn the ungodly who are living

s: honorable old age is not measured by length of time (nor by number of years)
q: For honorable old age is not that which stands in length of time, nor is its measure given by number of years,

s: honorable old age consists of unspotted life (understanding is gray hair to men)
q: but understanding is gray hair to men, and an unspotted life is ripe old age.

q: He was caught away, lest evil should change his understanding, or guile deceive his soul.

s: early death of the righteous is result of soul pleasing to the Lord (he hurried out of wickedness)

q: After this, they will become a dishonored carcass and a reproach among the dead forever;

s: final judgment of the ungodly has outcome memory perishes (dashed to the ground, laid waste, in anguish)
q: They will lie utterly waste. They will be in anguish and their memory will perish.

s: virtue is recognized before God (also before men)
q: because it is recognized both before God and before men.

s: God treats the ungodly with scorn (the Lord laughs them to scorn)
q: but the Lord will laugh them to scorn.

s: final judgment of the ungodly convicts by their lawless deeds (when sins are counted, they come with coward fear)
q: They will come with coward fear when their sins are counted. Their lawless deeds will convict them to their face.

s: virtue is imitated when present (people long after it when it departs)
q: When it is present, people imitate it. They long after it when it has departed.

s: virtue is victorious (crowned in triumph throughout all time in competition for undefiled prizes)
q: Throughout all time it marches, crowned in triumph, victorious in the competition for the prizes that are undefiled.

q: For even if they grow branches and flourish for a season, standing unsure, they will be shaken by the wind. They will be uprooted by the violence of winds.

s: brood of the ungodly (offspring) has fruit useless (never ripe, fit for nothing)
q: Their fruit will be useless, never ripe to eat, and fit for nothing.

s: brood of the ungodly (offspring) is witness against parents of unlawfully conceived children (unlawfully conceived children witness wickedness when investigated)
q: For unlawfully conceived children are witnesses of wickedness against parents when they are investigated.

s: righteous man has state at rest (even if he dies before his time)
q: But a righteous man, even if he dies before his time, will be at rest.

s: the righteous man stands before those who afflicted him (in great boldness)
q: Then the righteous man will stand in great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him

q: Therefore they will receive the crown of royal dignity and the diadem of beauty from the Lord’s hand

s: divine armor (the Lord's armor) has helmet impartial judgment
q: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and will wear impartial judgment as a helmet.

s: divine armor (the Lord's armor) has shield holiness (invincible)
q: He will take holiness as an invincible shield.

s: divine armor (the Lord's armor) has sword stern wrath (sharpened)
q: He will sharpen stern wrath for a sword.

s: creation fights with God (against his frenzied foes)
q: The universe will go with him to fight against his frenzied foes.

s: those who afflicted the righteous man regard righteous man as madness (his life, in their former view)
q: We fools considered his life madness, and his end without honor.

s: storms and elements (weapons against the wicked) is angered against the wicked (sea water)
q: The water of the sea will be angered against them.

s: the righteous man is counted among sons of God
q: How was he counted among sons of God? How is his lot among saints?

s: those who afflicted the righteous man went astray from the way of truth (confessed by them)
q: Truly we went astray from the way of truth.

s: those who afflicted the righteous man did not know the Lord's way (traveled trackless deserts)

q: Because the hope of the ungodly man is like chaff carried by the wind, and as foam vanishing before a tempest

s: the ungodly's fleeting prosperity passes away like a shadow (arrogance, riches and boasting)
q: Those things all passed away as a shadow, like a rumor that runs by,

s: the righteous live forever
q: But the righteous live forever.

s: the righteous have reward in God
q: Their reward is in the Lord, and the care for them with the Most High.

s: God is a Sovereign Lord of all
q: For the Sovereign Lord of all will not be impressed with anyone

s: Wisdom has quality radiant (does not fade)
q: Wisdom is radiant and doesn’t fade away

s: Wisdom is found by those who seek wisdom (easily seen by those who love her)
q: is easily seen by those who love her, and found by those who seek her.

s: Wisdom seeks those who seek wisdom (those worthy of her)
q: she herself goes around, seeking those who are worthy of her

s: Wisdom has beginning desire for instruction (her true beginning)
q: her true beginning is desire for instruction

s: Wisdom has fellowship with envy (none; envy excluded)
q: envy will have no fellowship with wisdom.

q: a stern judgment comes on those who are in high places.

s: immortality brings closeness to God
q: Immortality brings closeness to God.

s: God gives dominion to kings and rulers (the addressees) (source of their sovereignty)
q: because your dominion was given to you from the Lord, and your sovereignty from the Most High.

s: those who seek wisdom find Wisdom (early seekers find her at their gates)
q: He who rises up early to seek her won’t have difficulty, for he will find her sitting at his gates.

s: God made world (both small and great)
q: it is he who made both small and great, and cares about them all

s: God shows deference none (impartial toward greatness)
q: neither will he show deference to greatness

s: God cares about all people (small and great)
q: it is he who made both small and great, and cares about them all

s: kings and rulers (the addressees) is officer of God's kingdom
q: being officers of his kingdom

s: kings and rulers (the addressees) has failing did not judge rightly (as officers of God's kingdom)
q: you didn’t judge rightly, nor did you keep the law, nor did you walk according to God’s counsel.

s: kings and rulers (the addressees) faces judgment (stern, because in high places)
q: a stern judgment comes on those who are in high places.

s: kings and rulers (the addressees) is subject to strict scrutiny (as powerful)
q: the scrutiny that comes upon the powerful is strict.

s: speaker (the king, son of God's handmaid) is a mortal (like everyone else)

s: Wisdom has attribute more mobile than any motion
q: For wisdom is more mobile than any motion.

s: Wisdom is a breath of the power of God
q: For she is a breath of the power of God, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty.

s: Wisdom is a reflection of everlasting light
q: For she is a reflection of everlasting light, an unspotted mirror of the working of God, and an image of his goodness.

s: Wisdom has attribute purity (nothing defiled can enter her)
q: Therefore nothing defiled can find entrance into her.

q: Remaining in herself, she renews all things.

q: She is better than light.

q: but evil does not prevail against wisdom.

s: speaker (the king, son of God's handmaid) descends from one formed first (first-formed man)
q: am a descendant of one formed first and born of the earth.

s: God guides Wisdom (also corrects the wise)
q: he is one who guides even wisdom and who corrects the wise.

s: speaker (the king, son of God's handmaid) was formed in mother (narrator's mother) (womb, ten months)
q: I molded into flesh in the time of ten months in my mother’s womb

s: speaker (the king, son of God's handmaid) preferred Wisdom (over sceptres and thrones)
q: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones.

s: speaker (the king, son of God's handmaid) loves Wisdom (more than health and beauty)
q: I loved her more than health and beauty, and I chose to have her rather than light

s: speaker (the king, son of God's handmaid) possesses knowledge of the natural world (given by God)
q: For he himself gave me an unerring knowledge of the things that are, to know the structure of the universe and the operation of the elements;

s: kings has mortality and common human birth (no king had a different beginning)
q: For no king had a different beginning,

s: mortality and common human birth applies to mankind (one entrance into life and a common departure)
q: but all men have one entrance into life, and a common departure.

s: Wisdom is a architect of all things
q: for wisdom, that is the architect of all things, taught me.

s: Wisdom orders all things (does so well)
q: But she reaches from one end to the other with full strength, and orders all things well.

s: Wisdom gives good counsel (encourages in cares and grief)
q: knowing that she is one who would give me good counsel, and encourage me in cares and grief.

s: Wisdom is kin to immortality
q: how immortality is in kinship to wisdom

s: Wisdom possesses wealth that doesn't fail (in the labors of her hands)
q: in the labors of her hands is wealth that doesn’t fail

s: the speaker (narrator) loves Wisdom (since youth; sought her as bride)
q: I loved her and sought her from my youth. I sought to take her for my bride.

s: the speaker (narrator) is young
q: and honor in the sight of elders, though I am young.

s: the speaker (narrator) received a good soul (was a clever child)
q: Now I was a clever child, and received a good soul.

s: the speaker (narrator) has body (undefiled)
q: Or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.

s: the speaker (narrator) depends on God (God must give him wisdom)
q: I could not otherwise possess wisdom unless God gave her to me

s: God is Sovereign Lord of all
q: The Sovereign Lord of all loves her.

s: immortality is kin to Wisdom
q: how immortality is in kinship to wisdom

s: Wisdom lives with God (source of her noble birth)
q: She glorifies her noble birth by living with God.

s: Wisdom is loved by God (as Sovereign Lord of all)
q: The Sovereign Lord of all loves her.

s: Wisdom is initiated into knowledge of God
